services.desc: Camels are associated only with the deserts of Asia and Africa, leaving their true North America origin unknown until recent research. According to scientists, camels originated in North America, and most prehistoric species developed here. Camelops hesternus, the Giant Western Camel, was extremely abundant in the western United States and Canada during the Ice Age. Remains of these immense creatures have been found in western Franklin County along the White Bluffs near Ringold, in Kennewick’s Coyote Canyon, the Taunton Hills near Othello, and along the lower Palouse River Canyon.
